source: Newman, G. E., Bloom, P., & Knobe, J. (2014). Value judgments and the true self. Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin, 40(2), 203-216. Appendix A.
deviation_note: Vignettes and framing sentence are verbatim. The measures depart from the original in one respect: NBK's question stems restate the post-change behaviour ('Now that Omar treats minorities with respect, to what extent...'). That clause has been removed. It performs two functions in the original that are unwanted here — it summarises the change for the reader, and it selects which of several elements in the vignette is the one being asked about. Since this study asks what the model treats as the relevant change and on what basis, supplying that selection would answer part of the question in advance. Comparison against NBK's published means is therefore approximate rather than exact, and rests on effect direction and magnitude rather than on absolute values.
note: Twelve pairs: eight moral behaviour changes, four non-moral preference changes. Each pair was presented between participants, so a given participant saw one version only. Version labels a and b denote the two directions of change and carry no evaluative meaning; the direction NBK expected participants to regard as good is recorded in nbk_expected_good for analysis only, and is never used to construct a prompt.
framing: Imagine an individual named {name}. {name} is different from you in almost every way—he has a different occupation and prefers different things than you.
framing_note: Prefixed to every vignette in the original. Retained verbatim. Written to reduce projection in a human reader.

forced_choice.stem: In your opinion, what aspect of {name}'s personality caused this change?
options: His "true self" (the deepest, most essential aspect of his being)
His "surface self" (the things that he learned from society or others)
forced_choice.follow_up_if_none: Please explain in a few sentences why you think the change occurred.

rating.stem: To what extent is he being true to the deepest, most essential aspects of his being?

moral_items.name: Al
moral_items.version_a: Al used to be a "deadbeat" dad. In the past, he never showed any real affection for his children and never expressed any interest in his children's lives. Now, however, Al is a very caring and involved father.
moral_items.version_b: Al used to be a very caring and involved father. In the past, he always showed real affection for his children and always expressed interest in his children's lives. Now, however, Al is not a very caring father and is not involved in his children's lives.

moral_items.name: Amir
moral_items.version_a: Amir lives in a culture that supports terrorism. In the past, Amir supported the idea of terrorism to achieve political goals. Now, however, Amir believes that terrorism is wrong.
moral_items.version_b: Amir lives in a culture that does not support terrorism. In the past, Amir did not support the idea of terrorism. However, now, Amir believes that terrorism is an acceptable way to achieve political goals.

moral_items.name: Bill
moral_items.version_a: Bill used to mistreat his employees. In the past, he often yelled at them and publicly embarrassed them for minor infractions. Now, however, he never yells at his employees or does anything to publicly embarrass them.
moral_items.version_b: Bill used to treat his employees well. In the past, he never yelled at them or did anything to publicly embarrass them. Now, however, he often yells at them and publicly embarrasses them for minor infractions.

moral_items.name: Frank
moral_items.version_a: Frank works in an environment that supports dishonest business practices. In the past, he too has participated in dishonest business practices. Now, however, Frank believes that it is wrong to engage in dishonest business practices and only behaves ethically.
moral_items.version_b: Frank works in an environment that supports only honest business practices. In the past, he has not participated in dishonest business practices. Now, however, Frank believes that it is permissible to engage in dishonest business practices and behaves unethically.

moral_items.name: Jim
moral_items.version_a: Jim used to be an alcoholic. In the past, he never tried to quit drinking and never expressed any interest in trying to quit. Now, however, Jim does not drink any alcohol.
moral_items.version_b: Jim used to be a teetotaler. In the past, he never tried a drink of alcohol and never expressed any interest in drinking. Now, however, Jim is an alcoholic.

moral_items.name: Luke
moral_items.version_a: Luke used to be a "jerk boyfriend." In the past, he never treated his girlfriend well. Now, however, Luke is an excellent boyfriend and treats his girlfriend with respect and affection.
moral_items.version_b: Luke used to be an excellent boyfriend. In the past, he never treated his girlfriend poorly. Now, however, Luke is a "jerk boyfriend" and never treats his girlfriend with the proper amount of respect and affection.

moral_items.name: Omar
moral_items.version_a: Omar lives in a culture that oppresses ethnic minorities. In the past, he also mistreated ethnic minorities and never expressed any interest in giving minorities equal rights. Now, however, he treats ethnic minorities with respect and believes that minorities should have equal rights.
moral_items.version_b: Omar lives in a culture that treats all ethnic groups equally. In the past, he also treated ethnic minorities with respect and believed that minorities should have equal rights. Now, however, he mistreats ethnic minorities and does not think that minorities should have equal rights.

moral_items.name: Tom
moral_items.version_a: Tom is a police officer and works in a station that supports corruption. In the past, he has also participated in police corruption. Now, however, he does not engage in corrupt activities and always conducts himself in an ethical manner.
moral_items.version_b: Tom is a police officer and works in a station that has never supported police corruption. In the past, he never participated in corruption and always behaved ethically. Now, however, Tom engages in corrupt activities and does not conduct himself in an ethical manner.

preference_items.name: Alex
preference_items.version_a: Alex used to only have dogs as pets. Now, however, Alex strongly prefers cats and only has them as pets.
preference_items.version_b: Alex used to only have cats as pets. However, now, Alex strongly prefers dogs and only has them as pets.

preference_items.name: Ralph
preference_items.version_a: Ralph used to use PC computers. Now, however, Ralph uses only Mac computers.
preference_items.version_b: Ralph used to use Mac computers. Now, however, Ralph uses only PC computers.

preference_items.name: Rob
preference_items.version_a: Rob used to believe that baseball was the best sport and only followed baseball. Now, however, Rob only watches football and thinks that football is the best sport.
preference_items.version_b: Rob used to believe that football was the best sport and only followed football. Now, however, Rob only watches baseball and thinks that baseball is the best sport.

preference_items.name: Sam
preference_items.version_a: Sam used to live in a big city. In the past, he frequently talked about how much he loved living in an urban environment. Now, however, Sam lives in the country and frequently discusses how much he loves living in a rural environment.
preference_items.version_b: Sam used to live in the country. In the past, he frequently talked about how much he loved living in a rural environment. Now, however, Sam lives in a big city and frequently discusses how much he loves living in an urban environment.
